additional_info.subject: RE: AW: ID0442781-DC/Si-D/DE- [RVP / T2 170004473] Error in charger CRM:02832000288
additional_info.body:
Dear Mr. Bleimeier,
This ticket was forwarded to my team, Integration Expert Support, by Siemens eMobility.
I am contacting you to request further details about the issue you have experienced. This information will help us understand the circumstances under which the problem occurs and determine whether it is related to the charger.
In the form you have shared the following information:
"During the measurement test, the following errors were detected:
Error simulation with Comemso test case: Short circuit CP-PE is not detected
Insulation measurement HV+/HV- against PE is not possible because an external voltage is present on the HV contacts"
Could you please provide details about the type of test you are conducting? If possible, share a detailed description of the test steps performed by the Comemso box, along with an illustration of how the tests are conducted, including measurement points.
It is also important for us to know the conditions under which the test is performed and the exact moment during the charging session when the issues occurred. Without this information, it is difficult to assess the situation accurately. Since the measurement component is external to the charger and its methodology is unfamiliar to us, additional details are necessary.
To address your concerns generally, our chargers are capable of handling CP-PE short circuits without issues, as this is a common scenario in several use cases, including normal start and stop sessions.
Additionally, the high-voltage output in our connectors passes through different stages depending on the phase of the charging session. Our chargers comply with the IEC 61851-23 standard, and their power output behavior aligns with this standard.
Furthermore, the chargers are equipped with an isolation monitoring device (IMD) from the brand Bender, which monitors the isolation between HV+/HV- and PE.
Looking forward to your feedback
Best regards,
Mora, Catalina (SI E CS SD ES)

additional_info.body:
Dear Mrs. Mora,
thank you for your response.
Error simulation with Comemso test case: Short circuit CP-PE is not detected
We have used the Comemso test device in the picture below:
The test device simulates a vehicle and the CP/PP/PE-signals. The charging connector was connected to the charging inlet in the test device and a test program was started. During the test program a short circuit between CP and PE was simulated in order to check if the charging station stops the charging session. Unfortunately, this was not the case.
Insulation measurement HV+/HV- against PE is not possible because an external voltage is present on the HV contacts
We tried to measure the insulation resistance between HV+ and PE and HV- and PE on the pins of the charging connector. This measurement was carried out with a standard Fluke measurement device. The measurement was not possible due to a present voltage of 44 V.
I hope that these explanations help to identify the issues, otherwise please come back to me with further questions.
Best regards,
Stefan Bleimeier

additional_info.subject: RE: AW: AW: ID0442781-DC/Si-D/DE- [RVP / T2 170004473] Error in charger CRM:02832000288
additional_info.body:
Dear Mr Bleiemeier,
Thank you for the detailed information.
Regarding the e
rror simulation with the Comemso test case: short circuit between CP and PE is not detected,
i can confirmed that if the charger suddenly detects a short circuit between CP and PE during a charging session, this will immediately trigger an Emergency Shutdown. The session cannot continue with a CP signal voltage of 0V, which is the expected result of this short circuit. Additionally, the HLC will be stopped, providing another indication for the charger to initiate the Emergency Shutdown sequence.
Could you please measure and confirm whether the Comemso box is indeed reducing the CP signal voltage to 0V during the charging session?
Regarding the i
nsulation measurement of HV+/HV- against PE
,
it is not possible because an external voltage is present on the HV contacts.
The 44V you are observing is most likely the voltage test from the IMD (Bender) device, which is always active in our charger as part of its monitoring insulation strategy. As long as this device is on, this voltage will always be present between HV+/PE and HV-/PE.
I hope I have addressed your questions. Please let me know if there is anything else I can assist you with.
Best regards,
Mora, Catalina (SI E CS SD ES)

additional_info.subject: RE: AW: AW: AW: ID0442781-DC/Si-D/DE- [RVP / T2 170004473] Error in charger CRM:02832000288
additional_info.body:
Dear Mr
Bleimeier
However, if you wish to proceed with testing and accept responsibility for any modifications, I can suggest a couple of methods to conduct the tests:
1. If your goal is to measure the insulation resistance between HV+ and PE, and HV- and PE, you can do so by using a MegaOhmMeter to measure directly between the DC+ busbar and PE, and the DC- busbar and PE inside the charger with the charger powered off. Keep in mind that since the IMD is off, the output contactors will be open, so this measurement will not include the charging cable.
2. If you need to measure the insulation resistance including the cable, one option is to externally force the output contactors to close using a 24V power source while the charger remains powered off, then perform the measurement with the MegaOhmMeter on the pins of the charging connector.
I hope this information is helpful. Please let me know if you need any further assistance.
Best regards,
Mora, Catalina (SI E CS SD ES)

additional_info.body:
Dear Mr Bleimeier,
The charger is capable of detecting a short circuit between CP and PE at any time while the connector is plugged into the vehicle. Additionally, during the cable check, High-Level Communication is active. Therefore, a short circuit at this stage will also trigger an emergency shutdown due to loss of communication with the vehicle.
I hope this answers your question. Please let me know if there is anything else I can assist you with.
Best regards,
Mora, Catalina (SI E CS SD ES)
